title: Only the Mediocre Are Always at Their Best
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Opening with a Jean Giraudoux quotation, this piece explores why some team members deliberately choose mediocrity rather than lacking the ability to excel. It lists the real advantages mediocrity offers — less preparation, lower expectations, and a stress-free existence — that make it an attractive, deliberate choice for some. The article distinguishes this group from underperformers who genuinely need coaching, arguing leaders often waste effort trying to develop people who prefer the status quo. It closes by insisting good leaders never accept mediocrity as a legitimate choice, holding everyone to the same standard.
points: Some team members deliberately choose mediocrity rather than lacking the capacity to excel.
Mediocrity offers real advantages: less preparation, lower expectations, and a stress-free existence.
Leaders often waste effort trying to develop people who prefer the status quo of average performance.
Top performers come to disrespect colleagues who show no desire to improve, harming team cohesion.
The article insists good leaders never accept mediocrity as an acceptable choice, regardless of comfort with it.
quotes: French novelist Jean Giraudoux gave us that gem more than 80 years ago.
Savvy leaders come to understand that being mediocre has a host of advantages that are highly attractive to some team members.
The work-life balance of mediocre performers is usually quite good. And they like it that way.
Top-performing team members quickly come to disrespect colleagues who have no desire to improve.
Mediocrity is a virus best treated with unflinchingly high standards applied consistently.
